_about: HELD-OUT set 3 (D-184) for analyzer v3. Apps chosen and ground truth written on 2026-11-05 from the repos at the pinned commits, BEFORE v3 is implemented or run. v3's rules are the list fixed in docs/baseline/README.md section 4 (2026-10-27); the implementation must not add a rule outside that list because of these apps, and no rule is changed because of these results. expected_outcome is the real engine run on the expected fields (scripts/heldout3_expected.py), not the analyzer. Ground truth reviewed by 이진서 on 2026-11-05 with no value changed; it is now frozen.
selection: Six apps, none in apps.json / heldout.json / heldout2.json. Three probe v3's target (sub-folder and monorepo layouts, where extra folders must NOT be read as the app); three are ordinary shapes so v3 is also measured off its target.

apps.why: plain static site template with a gulp build; dist/ and src/ each carry their own package.json and webpack config

evidence.finding: only devDependencies (gulp, eslint, mocha); build = gulp build
ready-made static files; 404.html instead of an SPA fallback
template files for the user's project, not a second app

apps.notes: v3 trap: reading sub-folder manifests must not turn dist/ or src/ into a separate app.

apps.why: the Cloud Run sample service: Go net/http, PORT env, no storage; job/ and worker-pool/ are separate samples

evidence.finding: cloudevents sdk (received over HTTP); the rest is // indirect
builds /server from the root; job/ and worker-pool/ have their own Dockerfiles

apps.notes: v3 trap: job/ (a batch job) and worker-pool/ (non-HTTP) are other samples in the same repo, not parts of this service.

apps.why: client/ (React, Vite) + backend/ (Express) built into one image; MySQL when MYSQL_HOST is set, else a SQLite file

evidence.finding: final stage copies the client build into backend/src/static; CMD node src/index.js
app.listen(3000): port is hard-coded, no env var
mysql:9.3 with a volume; MYSQL_HOST/USER/PASSWORD/DB for the backend

apps.notes: One process serves the screen and the API, so SERVER_APP (not STATIC_PLUS_API). Without MYSQL_HOST it writes a local SQLite file (in_memory_state). MySQL is not a platform engine (OTHER). MySQL makes it UNSUPPORTED; the fixed port 3000 would be the next blocker (INCOMPATIBLE).

apps.why: vote (Flask) + result (Node, socket.io) + worker (.NET) + Redis + Postgres

evidence.finding: services vote, result, worker built here; redis and postgres images

apps.notes: Out of scope (one service per environment). v3 trap: reading vote/, result/, worker/ manifests must lead to multi-service, not to one merged app.

apps.why: Excalidraw's collaboration relay: socket.io rooms, nothing stored

evidence.finding: process.env.PORT || 80; rooms live in the socket.io server's memory (no adapter)

apps.notes: Rooms are per process: two instances would split a room, so in_memory_state is true even though nothing is written to disk.

apps.why: Heroku's Django sample: SQLite locally, Postgres via DATABASE_URL in production; no Dockerfile

evidence.finding: django, gunicorn, dj-database-url, whitenoise; psycopg commented out
Greeting model written by the /db page

apps.notes: Judgment call for the reviewer: the production path is Postgres (the driver line is commented out until a DB is attached), so POSTGRES. No Dockerfile: an image must be built first (buildpacks, project.toml).
